lines.text: Does eye black actually do anything?
It makes you look like a raccoon.
It's war paint! It's supposed to look scary!
The idea is, sunlight hits your cheekbones...
and bounces right up into your eyes. That's glare.
Glare washes out the ball against a bright sky.
Black grease soaks up that light instead of bouncing it.
So it's sunglasses... for your face?
Tiny, greasy sunglasses. Sure.
In 2003, Yale doctors tested it in bright sunlight.
With the grease, people saw contrast a little better.
Told you. Science says I'm scary.
Science says you're slightly less blinded.
And those stickers with the logos? They didn't help at all.
My stickers are a lie?
They scored the same as a smear of petroleum jelly.
Grape jelly on my face. Game day.
Wrong jelly.
Players used to smear on burnt cork. The grease is the upgrade.
It works. A little. And now you know.
Still looks scary though. So real question...
